title: Showers expected in several areas today
byline: Showers or thundershowers may occur at a few places in the Sabaragamuwa province and in the Galle, Matara, Kalutara and Nuwara-Eliya districts during the evening or night, the Department of Meteorology stated.

title: Trump’s signature to appear on US dollars in first for sitting president
byline: Donald Trump is set to become the first sitting US president to have his signature on US banknotes, the Treasury Department has announced.

title: Trump extends pause on striking Iran’s energy plants by 10 days
byline: US President Donald Trump on Thursday (Mar 26) pushed back his deadline for strikes on Iran’s energy assets to Apr 6, saying it was at Tehran’s request and that talks were “going very well”.

title: Global oil prices, which had climbed on Thursday, drop after Trump’s latest comments
byline: The Nasdaq index, where many tech firms are listed, dropped nearly 2.4%, weighed down in part by a sharp slide in sales of Meta shares, after back-to-back juries found against the company in closely watched court cases in the US.

title: Trump weighs sending another 10,000 ground troops to the Middle East, WSJ reports
byline: The Pentagon is looking at sending up to 10,000 additional ground troops to the Middle East ⁠to give President Donald Trump more military options even as he weighs peace talks with Tehran,...

title: Nepal to swear in ex-rapper as new prime minister
byline: Rapper-turned-politician Balendra Shah will be sworn in as Nepal’s prime minister after a landslide victory in the country’s first election since last year’s youth-led protests.

title: India cuts special excise duties on petrol, diesel
byline: India slashed its special excise duties on petrol and diesel, as fuel prices stay volatile with supplies choked by the Iran war.

title: ‘Harry Potter’ series embroiled in controversy as Snape actor faces death threats, online abuse
byline: Harry Potter TV series is already under tight scrutiny even before its release as it lands in one controversy after the other.

title: Three arrested for illegal fuel hoarding in separate raids
byline: Three suspects have been arrested for allegedly hoarding fuel illegally in separate raids conducted across several areas of the island.

title: Netflix raises subscription prices across all plans in US
byline: Netflix has increased prices on all its plans in the U.S., as the streaming giant pushes into new programming formats such as video podcasts and live sporting events.

title: Six killed in separate road accidents across the island
byline: A total of six individuals have died in several road accidents reported in different parts of the island, police said.

title: Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody arrives at Colombo High Court
byline: The Minister of Energy, Kumara Jayakody, has arrived at the Colombo High Court, said Ada Derana reporter.

title: Apple plans to open Siri to rival AI services, Bloomberg News reports
byline: Apple plans to open its Siri voice assistant to rival artificial intelligence services beyond its current partnership with ChatGPT, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

title: Israel completes ‘wave of strikes in the heart of Tehran’, says IDF
byline: The Israeli military says it has “completed a wave of strikes in the heart of Tehran”.

title: Drone attack targets Kuwait’s main port, authorities say
byline: Kuwait said Friday that its main commercial port, Shuwaikh Port, was targeted in a “hostile” drone attack, causing material damage but no injuries.

title: Passenger arrested at BIA for attempt to smuggle ornamental plants
byline: A passenger was arrested by Sri Lanka Customs officials at Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in Katunayake this morning (27) for attempting to smuggle a consignment of ornamental plants into the country from Thailand.

title: Opposition Leader urges Sri Lanka to ‘follow suit’ after India’s fuel duty cuts
byline: Following India’s decision to cut special excise duties on petrol and diesel, Sri Lanka’s Opposition Leader, Sajith Premadasa, has urged the government to do the same on fuel prices here and provide relief to the public.

title: Appeals and objections called for 2nd phase of ‘Aswesuma’ Scheme
byline: The Welfare Benefits Board has issued a notice regarding the publication of the qualified beneficiary list under the second phase of the Aswesuma Welfare Benefits Payment Scheme, as well as the opportunity to submit appeals and objections.

title: ‘Defence shall persist as long as it is needed’, Iranian FM Araghchi at UN
byline: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi on Friday slammed the United States and Israel for the attacks on civilian infrastructure in Iran, most notably the Minab Elementary Girls’ school which killed over 160 people.

title: IRGC says ships attempting to transit via Strait of Hormuz will face ‘harsh measures’
byline: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Friday that the Strait of Hormuz is closed and any transit through the waterway will face “harsh measures.”

title: 38,000MT of diesel and petrol to arrive from India tomorrow
byline: A combined shipment of 38,000 metric tons of diesel and petrol is scheduled to arrive at the Colombo Harbour from India tomorrow (29), the Indian High Commission confirmed.

title: Luxury private bus catches fire on expressway; No Injuries reported
byline: A luxury private passenger transport bus traveling from Colombo to Kataragama has reportedly caught fire near the Welipanna interchange on the Southern Expressway this afternoon (27).

title: Oscars to leave Hollywood in 2029: Academy
byline: The Oscars will leave Hollywood after celebrating their centenary, organizers said Thursday, as they announced a long-term deal to hold the gala in downtown Los Angeles.

title: Suspect arrested with heroin, ‘Ice’ and cocaine worth over Rs. 50 mln
byline: A suspect has been arrested in the Sapugaskanda area for the possession of a large consignment of narcotics valued at over Rs. 50 million.

title: IDF issues immediate evacuation warning in Arak, central Iran
byline: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has issued an urgent warning to people in parts of Arak, the capital of the Markazi province in central Iran.

title: Ex-rapper Balendra Shah sworn in as Nepal prime minister after sweeping election win
byline: Rapper-turned-politician Balendra Shah was sworn in as prime minister of Nepal on Friday, tasked with restoring political stability and creating jobs in the poor Himalayan nation long troubled by fragile governments and weak growth prospects.

title: Fuel delivery to be restored following CPC agreement on transport charges
byline: Fuel delivery will be restored from tomorrow (28), following the agreement by the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) to increase intercity fuel transportation charges by 25%, the Fuel Transporter Bowser Owners’ Association said.

title: Ex-minister Keheliya and others found guilty, fined over medicine procurement scandal
byline: The Supreme Court of Sri Lanka has ruled that former Health Minister Keheliya Rambukwella and several others violated Fundamental Rights of the public through the procurement of health supplies from an unregistered company, in breach of standard procurement procedures, under the 2022 Indian Credit Line.

title: No price increase for confectionery products until May - LCMA
byline: The Lanka Confectionery Manufacturers Association (LCMA) has announced that prices of biscuits, ice cream, chocolate, and other confectionery products will not be increased until May.

title: Iran-linked hackers claim breach of FBI director’s personal email; DOJ official confirms break-in
byline: Iran-linked hackers have publicly claimed the breach of FBI Director Kash Patel’s personal inbox, publishing photographs of the director and his purported resume to the internet.

title: Met. Dept warns of continued hot weather in Sri Lanka until May
byline: The Department of Meteorology of Sri Lanka has announced that the prevailing warm weather conditions are expected to persist until May.

title: Warm weather advisory issued for several provinces
byline: A warm weather advisory has been issued for residents of the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, Eastern, North-western, Northern and North-central provinces and in Monaragala district.

title: Crowds gather at ID Office despite suspension of services due to system failure
byline: Despite the suspension of all public services, including the one-day service, due to a sudden technical failure in the computer system of the Department for Registration of Persons (ID Office), crowds have once again gathered at the premises today (27).

title: Taylor Swift and ‘Showgirl’ dominate iHeartRadio Music Awards
byline: Music superstar Taylor Swift scored a leading seven trophies at the iHeartRadio Music Awards on Thursday including artist of the year and best pop album for the upbeat record ‘‘The Life of a Showgirl.’’

title: Railway Dept. issues notice on Ambepussa–Alawwa train services
byline: The Department of Railways has issued an announcement regarding the restriction of train operations to a single track between Ambepussa and Alawwa to facilitate permanent repairs on the Bujjomuwa Bridge.

title: Woman abducted and thrown into well in Batti: Another suspect arrested
byline: Sri Lanka Police have uncovered further details regarding the recent incident in the Nellikkadu area of Batticaloa, where an abducted woman was rescued from an abandoned well.

title: Indictments served on Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody, granted bail
byline: Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody has been served indictments before the Colombo High Court in connection with allegations of corruption, said Ada Derana reporter.

title: Suspension of tuition classes on Wednesdays a request, not an order: official
byline: The Commissioner General of Essential Services, Prabath Chandrakeerthi has requested teachers to suspend all tuition classes held on Wednesdays.

title: CAA conducts special raids against errant traders ahead of festive season
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) says a special programme has been implemented to safeguard consumers ahead of the upcoming festive season.

title: Water levels drop rapidly in several reservoirs in N’Eliya
byline: The water levels in several reservoirs across the Nuwara Eliya District have dropped rapidly due to the prevailing dry weather conditions.

title: AG not representing Speaker in case over ex-Deputy Sec-Gen of Parliament’s suspension
byline: The Attorney General has not represented the Speaker, who is named as a respondent in the petition filed challenging the suspension of former Deputy Secretary General of Parliament Chaminda Kularatne, while President’s Counsel K. Kanag-Isvaran today (27) appeared before the Court of Appeal on behalf of the Speaker.

title: Health Secretary warns of increased health risks amidst rising temperatures
byline: Sri Lanka’s health authorities have warned that a significant rise in environmental temperatures is currently being experienced, primarily due to a combination of climatic factors.

title: Sri Lanka CERT conducts cyber safety awareness program for MPs
byline: The Sri Lanka Computer Emergency Readiness Team (Sri Lanka CERT) conducted a Cyber Safety Awareness Program for the Members of Parliament of Sri Lanka, with the objective of enhancing awareness on the secure and responsible use of digital technologies, particularly in the context of national governance.

title: UNDP donates two modern mobile mercury analyzers to CAA
byline: In order to ensure consumer safety, two modern mobile mercury analyzers worth Rs. 1.8 million have been donated to the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) under the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

title: Karapitiya Hospital to implement smart token OPD system, plans future upgrade to QR technology
byline: The new digitalization program introduced at the Outpatient Department (OPD) of the Karapitiya National Hospital, Galle came under the special inspection of Deputy Minister of Health, Dr. Hansaka Wijemuni, today (27).

title: Iran says two nuclear facilities attacked
byline: Two nuclear-related facilities have been attacked in Iran, but there has been no release of radioactive material, Iranian state media says.
